title: UP Police Cyber Security Internship 2026 — 15 Days at Amroha | Gautam Kumar Maurya
description: A day-by-day case file of the Amroha Police Cyber Security Internship Program (APCSIP-2026), 10–22 June 2026: 13 field logs, 12 domains taught by India's top cyber security experts, 45+ officers and experts met, and the Best Content Creator award.

programme.name: Amroha Police Cyber Security Internship Program (APCSIP) 2026
programme.host: Uttar Pradesh Police — Amroha Police Cyber Crime Cell
programme.location: Shri Venkateshwara University, Amroha, Uttar Pradesh, India
programme.role: Cyber security intern — field log recorder
instructors: DSP Anjali Kataria (Amroha Cyber Crime Cell)
Rakshit Tandon (senior consultant and advisor to law enforcement)
Amit Dubey (cyber crime investigator and author)
programme.outcome: Programme completion certificate and the Best Content Creator award, presented by DSP Anjali Kataria at the valedictory on 22 June 2026, for the daily field logs published on LinkedIn throughout the fellowship.

days.label: Log 01 · Wed 10 Jun 2026
days.title: Reporting, welcome kit and orientation
days.summary: Arrived at Shri Venkateshwara University and reported to the APCSIP registration desk. Credential verification, the official welcome kit, the internship badge and the offer letter — then an afternoon briefing on discipline, attendance and assessment parameters.

days.label: Log 02 · Thu 11 Jun 2026
days.title: Inauguration and the shape of the threat
days.summary: The formal opening with Amroha Police officials and the programme's cyber security experts. Keynotes mapped the emerging cyber threat picture in Uttar Pradesh — financial scam networks, phishing ecosystems and how local cyber cells plug into the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.

days.label: Log 03 · Fri 12 Jun 2026
days.title: Cyber psychology, then the OSINT bench
days.summary: Morning on the human layer: urgency, fear and authority pretexts — how fraudsters actually manipulate victims. Afternoon on the OSINT bench with Maltego, Shodan, Google dorks, DeHashed and FotoForensics, finishing with an audit of our own digital footprints.

days.label: Log 04 · Sat 13 Jun 2026
days.title: Cyber law, research method and AI on the bench
days.summary: The legal spine of the programme: India's IT Act 2000 and Section 66 offences, digital evidence rules and forensic case reporting. Afternoon paired ML and generative AI for threat-pattern recognition and log anomaly detection, then a career panel on CEH, CISSP and DFIR paths.

days.label: Log 05 · Sun 14 Jun 2026
days.title: Malware analysis and evidence imaging
days.summary: Android malware from the inside: packaging, decompiling APKs, mapping command-and-control servers and disciplining analysis inside sandboxes. The afternoon was pure forensics — imaging with write-blockers, chain-of-custody rules and MD5/SHA-256 hash verification.

days.label: Log 06 · Mon 15 Jun 2026
days.title: SOC operations and bug bounty
days.summary: A full day at the monitoring desk: SOC architecture, event correlation, SIEM and EDR platforms, live alert triage in Wazuh, Elastic, Wireshark and VirusTotal. The afternoon flipped to the attacker's view — subdomain enumeration, API endpoint auditing and responsible disclosure via HackerOne and Bugcrowd.

days.label: Log 07 · Tue 16 Jun 2026
days.title: DPDP compliance and following the mules
days.summary: DPDP Act 2023 obligations — consent, purpose limitation, retention — read from an investigator's seat. The money trail followed next: mule accounts, RBI and I4C guidance, SWIFT CSP and reconstructing a fraud chain from the first UPI debit to the last withdrawal.

days.label: Log 08 · Wed 17 Jun 2026
days.title: Blockchain, crypto and real police cases
days.summary: Blockchain structure, key cryptography, contract flaws and 51% attacks — then real Section 91 CrPC case studies on evidence handling and wallet tracing, walked through by officers from live investigations.

days.label: Log 09 · Thu 18 Jun 2026
days.title: Privacy as a fundamental right
days.summary: The morning belonged to K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India — the Supreme Court ruling that made privacy a fundamental right — and what it means for ethics in emerging tech. The afternoon was a closed briefing on handling classified threat intelligence, officer discretion and professional ethics.

days.label: Log 10 · Fri 19 Jun 2026
days.title: Offensive security and the dark web
days.summary: Thinking like the attacker, legally: system enumeration, directory brute-forcing, port scanning, web security headers and cross-origin configurations. Then the dark web — Tor onion routing, entry/middle/exit nodes, hidden service directories and cyber kill-chain mapping.

days.label: Log 11 · Sat 20 Jun 2026
days.title: Reverse engineering — and the award announcement
days.summary: The deepest technical day: malware detonated inside isolated FlareVM and REMnux virtual machines, process trees monitored with Process Hacker and Wireshark, behaviour documented like evidence, plus physical chip-off extraction from damaged devices. In the afternoon the Best Content Creator award was announced.

days.label: Log 12 · Sun 21 Jun 2026
days.title: Mobile acquisition, cyber hygiene and yoga
days.summary: Hands-on mobile forensics — acquisition types, app artefacts and the discipline of custody — alongside cyber-hygiene drills for police teams. The day closed with a session on physical and mental resilience, with yoga, for officers who carry case stress daily.

days.label: Log 13 · Mon 22 Jun 2026
days.title: Valedictory defence and the certificate
days.summary: The final defence: technical findings, OSINT case files and CDR analysis reports presented before the review panel. Then the graduation — the official APCSIP-2026 completion certificate, the Best Content Creator honour presented by DSP Anjali Kataria, and the last set of group photographs with the officers.

faq.q: What was the UP Police cyber security internship (APCSIP-2026)?
faq.a: APCSIP-2026 was a 15-day cyber security fellowship run by the Amroha Police Cyber Crime Cell, Uttar Pradesh Police, from 10 to 22 June 2026 at Shri Venkateshwara University, Amroha. Gautam Kumar Maurya was selected through an eight-gate pipeline including a 50-question cyber aptitude exam.

faq.q: What did Gautam Kumar Maurya do during the fellowship?
faq.a: Twelve operational days covering 12 domains — OSINT, mobile forensics, CDR/IPDR analysis, malware analysis, SOC and SIEM operations, UPI fraud tracing, dark web investigation, web and network auditing, IT Act law, cyber psychology and blockchain forensics — documented in 13 dated field logs, 12 of which were published on LinkedIn.

The faculty included Rakshit Tandon, Amit Dubey, DSP Anjali Kataria of the Amroha Cyber Crime Cell, and specialists such as Saumay Srivastava, Yugal Pathal, Nitin Pandey, Kailash D Agrawal, Pakhi Garg, Yash Chavhan and Manoj Kushwaha — more than 45 officers, experts and coordinators in total.

faq.q: What award did Gautam Kumar Maurya receive?
faq.a: The Best Content Creator award at the APCSIP-2026 valedictory on 22 June 2026, presented by DSP Anjali Kataria, along with the official completion certificate — recognition for the daily field logs published on LinkedIn throughout the fellowship.

Applications opened in May 2026, followed by a screening shortlist on 21–22 May, a 50-question multiple-choice cyber aptitude exam on 24 May, an offer letter, document verification and reporting at Amroha on 10 June 2026.

faq.q: How can I verify the internship and the award?
faq.a: The 12 LinkedIn field logs linked from each entry on this page, the certificate image in the award section, the roles ledger entry GKM-EXP-UPP-2026 and the achievements dossier entry up-police-best-content-creator-2026.
